summary: Give the nightly backup a reader: backup-status reports the scheduled wrapper's run markers, and the scaffold owns the backup timer instead of retiring it.
details: yawn.vps commit bc4f29e fixes two defects in bin/backup-status: the last-backup section asked the receipt for created_utc, a field menhir-backup-local never writes (the field is checked_utc), so it always printed (missing); and the final section read the retired job-runner status file and printed (no backup job recorded) forever. It now reports scheduled-backup-last-run.json and, when present, scheduled-backup-failure.json, the markers written by /usr/local/sbin/menhir-scheduled-backup on every run. Menhir commits 23f8c11, c224548 and 8c5015c make the host scaffold the owner of that wrapper and of menhir-backup.service and menhir-backup.timer, which the scaffold had retired as legacy since its first commit while its own audit demanded a backup fresher than 24 hours; the scaffold is not a release artifact and was installed separately on 2026-09-13, but the release's backup-status now depends on the markers it produces. No other release artifact changes; images are inherited from release 0.2.0-13 unchanged.
operator_impact: backup-status gains a final section describing the last scheduled nightly run and any standing failure. No runtime, ingress, secret or privilege change.
